paper.title: Construction and Notation of Convex Polygon Triangulation Based on Ballot Problem
paper.abstract: In this paper we provide a new way for constructing and storing the convex polygon triangulations. The main motivation for the presented method is derived from two combinatorial problems: ballot problem and problem of lattice path. The method is derived upon the so-called movement through polygon. The movement is defined on ballot records and validity of the lattice path through the grid. We give two algorithms: Triangulation to ballot and Ballot to triangulation. Also, we give a method to make coding for a ballot record or the corresponding triangulation even more compact using a stack. All mentioned algorithms are implemented in the Java programming language.

artifact_assessment.evidence: Java applications for both methods can be downloaded from: http://muzafers.uninp.edu.rs/triangulation/Ballot.rar and http://muzafers.uninp.edu.rs/triangulation/Hurtado.rar

flag_details.FORMALISM_THEATER: Level 2 paper (an encoding of convex-polygon triangulations as ballot strings and stack permutations, with no complexity analysis) whose formal apparatus exceeds the Level 2 bound (1 definition, 2 propositions, 2 proofs = 16 > 15) and fails the necessity test: Propositions 2.1 and 3.1 re-prove textbook Catalan-number counts that the algorithms do not depend on, Definition 3.1 formalises a cyclic vertex distance that amounts to 'the two vertices are adjacent', and the ballot string is written as a set b = {b1, ..., b2n}.
flag_details.EXCESSIVE_SELF_CITATION: 3 of 7 references ([5], [6], [7]) are by the authors (SCR = 43%). All three concern convex polygon triangulation and are topically related, but the ratio exceeds 30%.
flag_details.NO_LIMITATIONS: No limitations section and no inline acknowledgment of constraints; the conclusion lists only advantages, and the finding that generation is slower than Hurtado-Noy is reported without discussion of its implications.

verdict.summary: Modest combinatorial encoding of convex polygon triangulations via ballot records and stack permutations, with downloadable Java code and a timing/memory comparison; re-proves known Catalan counts as propositions and has a 43% self-citation ratio over a seven-item reference list.

papers.provenance:
## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** Bijective encoding of convex (n+2)-gon triangulations as ballot records (balanced A/B strings), decoding back to triangulations by a 'movement through the polygon', and compacting ballot records into stack permutations (SVBs); empirical comparison with the Hurtado-Noy tree method.
**Level:** 2 (Low)
**Rationale:** The correspondences between ballot sequences, lattice paths, stack permutations and triangulations are classical Catalan-family bijections. The paper contributes procedural algorithms for one such bijection and a storage comparison, with no complexity analysis, no correctness proof of the bijection, and no new mathematical result. Level 3 requires a novel algorithm with complexity analysis; defaulting low gives Level 2.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 1 (Definition 3.1, cyclic distance d(p,q))
- Theorems: 2 (Propositions 2.1 and 3.1)
- Proofs: 2
- Equations: about 5 (binomial counts (1)-(2), Segner recurrence (3), Cn = Tn+2 (4), the substitution in Proposition 3.1)

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 1x2 + 2x3 + 2x4 = 16
Expected range (Level 2): 0-15
Ratio: 1.07x upper bound

**Assessment:** Disproportionate for the level, and the elements fail the necessity test. Proposition 2.1 (ballot records are counted by Catalan numbers) and Proposition 3.1 (the number of 'movements through triangulation' is Catalan) are standard results from the cited Koshy monograph; the Proposition 3.1 proof is an informal counting argument that defers to the authors' own paper [7]. Neither result is used to establish correctness of Algorithms 1-4, which is the property that would actually need proof. Definition 3.1 introduces d(p,q) = min{|p-q|, v-|p-q|} only to test whether a side is an outer edge (d = 1) or a diagonal (d > 1), which is the plain-English test 'are the endpoints adjacent'. The ballot string is written in set notation, b = {b1, ..., b2n}, for what is an ordered sequence.

### Issues
- The central claim, that Algorithms 1 and 3 are mutually inverse and that every ballot record yields a valid triangulation, is illustrated by examples (AABABB, ABAABB) but never proved.
- Algorithm 1's step 2.2.1 ('If there are two successive characters B in b then return for one more node back') is ambiguous about which pair of B's is meant.
- Algorithm 2 delegates intersection testing to Java3D's Triangulator and Polygon.intersects, so the geometric part is library code.

---

## Citation Analysis

The reference list is short (7 items). References [5], [6], [7] are by subsets of the author team (Saračević, Stanimirović, Krtolica, Mašović), giving SCR = 3/7 = 43%. All three are on convex polygon triangulation (an implementation paper, a block method in this same journal, and a Catalan decomposition paper) and are topically relevant (similarity well above 0.5), so no irrelevant self-citation. The ratio is nonetheless excessive, partly a consequence of the thin related-work coverage: no other encoding or ranking schemes for triangulations or Catalan objects are discussed beyond Hurtado-Noy.

---

## Structural Analysis

Claims of efficiency are supported by Tables 2 and 3 (CPU time and memory for v = 5..16), and the reported differences are arithmetically consistent with Table 2. The tables show the ballot method is slower at generation but cheaper in storage, and the text reports this honestly. Measurement methodology is thin: single runs, no variance, and the memory figures for the ballot method record only the SVB output while the comparison is framed as overall memory savings. No limitations are acknowledged. The authors provide links to downloadable Java applications for both their method and the Hurtado-Noy baseline; there is no separate dataset, the triangulations being generated by the code.

No instructions addressed to an assessor or reviewer appear in the text.

---

## Conclusion

A small applied combinatorics contribution: a workable encoding and storage scheme for convex polygon triangulations, with code released, which is a genuine strength. The formal content restates known Catalan identities rather than proving properties of the new algorithms, which pushes the formalism past what a Level 2 contribution warrants, and the self-citation ratio is high on a short reference list. Both of these trigger disqualifying flags under the framework.

paper.title: Sugeno Measures on the Code Space
paper.abstract: One considers a finite set X (the alphabet), the code space X^∞ of all sequences formed with elements (letters) from the alphabet X and B the Borel sets of X^∞. A concrete representation of all Sugeno measures on B is given. This representation is, heuristically speaking, matricial, being inspired by the concrete representation of all probabilities on B.

artifact_assessment.evidence: no availability statement or link in the text

flag_details.ELEVATED_FORMALISM: Level 3 paper with formalism complexity of about 65 (8 definitions x2 + 7 lemmas/theorems x3 + 7 proofs x4), between the Level 3 upper bound of 40 and twice that bound. The formalism is necessary for a measure-theoretic representation result; the flag records proportion relative to the modest depth of the results, which compose known bijections.
flag_details.ELEVATED_SELF_CITATION: 3 of 14 references ([3], [4], [5]) include the first author (SCR = 21%). [5] on countable lambda-measures is directly related; [3] and [4] on Martin-Löf random sequences are cited only as examples of where the code space appears and are marginally related.

verdict.summary: Pure measure-theory paper giving a 'matricial' representation of all Sugeno (lambda-) measures on the Borel sets of the code space by composing Wang's lambda-measure/probability bijection with the classical distribution representation; formalism is genuine and correct in outline, though heavy relative to the depth of the results.

papers.provenance:
## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** Representation of Sugeno lambda-measures on the Borel sigma-algebra of the code space X^N (X a finite alphabet) by sequences of arrays ('lambda-distributions') satisfying product consistency conditions, plus a characterisation of measures that are lambda-measures for every lambda (Dirac measures) and the non-injectivity of the global correspondence.
**Level:** 3 (Medium)
**Rationale:** The paper proves new but modest properties within an established theory: Theorem 3.5 is obtained by composing three known bijections (a logarithmic change of variable L_lambda, the classical correspondence T_0 between consistent distributions and probabilities on cylinders, and Wang's bijection V_lambda), and Theorems 3.2, 3.3 and 3.10 characterise the overlap of the families S_lambda. This is substantive extension of a theoretical framework (Level 3), not a complexity, soundness or universality result.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 8 (monotone measure, lambda-rule, lambda-measure, Sugeno measure, prefix order and cylinders, 0-distribution, Definition 3.4 lambda-distribution, Definition 3.6 general distribution; Definition 3.8 is an operational map definition counted with them)
- Theorems: 7 (Lemma 3.1, Theorems 3.2, 3.3, 3.5, Lemma 3.7, Theorems 3.9, 3.10)
- Proofs: 7
- Equations: numerous, all part of definitions or proofs

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 8x2 + 7x3 + 7x4 = 65 (up to 69 if Definition 3.8 and the Dirac-measure definition are counted separately)
Expected range (Level 3): 10-40
Ratio: about 1.6x upper bound

**Assessment:** Elevated but not theater. Every formal element passes the necessity test: in a measure-theory paper the definitions and proofs are the contribution, and there is no implementation for them to stand in for. Set notation here is native measure-theoretic language, not list manipulation. The count is high mainly because the paper proves small auxiliary facts (Lemma 3.1, Lemma 3.7, Theorem 3.9) in full.

### Issues
- Theorem 3.3 writes the intersection over lambda in (-1, inf), including lambda = 0 via S_0 = M, while Theorem 3.2 is stated over (-1/a, inf); the bookkeeping is consistent but awkwardly signposted ('write here S_0 = M').
- Several typographical slips ('mu(T) = = a', 'a_lambda(...) = = (lambda+1)^...', the sum index n instead of p in the proof of Lemma 3.7) do not affect correctness.
- Theorem 3.10's final claim that T^{-1}({delta_x}) equals the set of constructed distributions relies on the uniqueness part of Theorem 3.5 for each lambda; this is correct but stated without that justification.

---

## Citation Analysis

14 references. Self-citations: [3] and [4] (Calude and Chiţescu on Martin-Löf random sequences) and [5] (Chiţescu, Stănică, Plăviţu on countable lambda-measures with preassigned values). SCR = 3/14 = 21%. [5] is closely related (lambda-measures, similarity above 0.5). [3] and [4] are cited only to illustrate that the code space is used in the theory of random sequences; their topical similarity to Sugeno measures is marginal (about 0.3-0.5) but not unrelated, since both concern measures on the code space. No ring pattern is visible. The remaining references are standard monographs (Wang-Klir, Halmos, Dinculeanu, Barnsley, Falconer) and the original Sugeno and Wang sources, all relevant.

---

## Structural Analysis

Every claimed result is accompanied by a proof, so the claim-evidence ratio is high. The introduction's motivating claims about superadditive and subadditive measures modelling synergy and inhibition are unsupported by citation but peripheral. No limitations are acknowledged; the closing section lists only directions for future work (Choquet and Sugeno integrals, cellular automata). As a pure theory paper it has nothing to release; artifact availability is recorded as none with relevant set to false.

No instructions addressed to an assessor or reviewer appear in the text.

---

## Conclusion

A competent, short contribution to generalized measure theory. The main representation theorem follows quite directly from composing a logarithmic reparametrisation with two known bijections, so the novelty is modest and the formal apparatus is heavy for that depth, which is recorded as elevated formalism. The formalism itself is legitimate and necessary, the proofs are sound in outline, and the citations are mostly appropriate, with a mildly elevated self-citation ratio.
